message.content: The largest exoplanet that astronomers have confirmed so far is roughly **2½ × the radius of Jupiter** and has a mass of about **15–20 Jupiter masses**. One of the best‑studied examples is the planet orbiting the young star HD 100546, whose radius is about 2.5 R_J and whose mass is estimated at ≈ 15 M_J. This object sits right on the boundary between giant planets and low‑mass brown dwarfs, so it’s sometimes classified as a “super‑Jupiter” rather than a true planet.
